packets.title: S007 Al-Araf CP01 vv001-025
paragraphs: S007 — AL-AʿRĀF — CP01
Unit: 7:1–25 (25 verses)
Surah tag: Meccan by the traditional list; 206 verses
Translations: Arabic primary. Core five on split loci.
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

Alif lām mīm ṣād. A Book sent down to you — let there be no ḥaraj in your breast from it — that you may warn by it, and a reminder for the believers. Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord and do not follow protectors besides Him. Little do you remember. How many a town We destroyed; Our violence came to them at night or while they napped at noon. Their cry when Our violence came was only: we were ẓālimīn. We will question those to whom it was sent and We will question the messengers. We will recount to them with knowledge; We were not absent. The weighing that day is the truth. Whose scales are heavy — they are the successful. Whose scales are light — they are the ones who lost their souls for that they used to wrong Our signs. We have established you in the earth and placed for you in it livelihoods. Little do you thank.

We created you, then fashioned you, then said to the angels: prostrate to Adam. They prostrated except Iblīs; he was not of the prostrators. He said: what prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you? He said: I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay. He said: get down from it; it is not for you to grow proud in it; get out; you are of the humbled. He said: respite me to the day they are raised. He said: you are of those respited. He said: because You have sent me astray I will sit for them on Your straight path. Then I will come at them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left; You will not find most of them thankful. He said: get out of it, disgraced, banished. Whoever of them follows you, I will fill Jahannam with you all. And O Adam, dwell you and your wife in the garden and eat from where you will, but do not approach this tree lest you be ẓālimīn. Then Satan whispered to them to show them what was hidden from them of their nakedness, and he said: your Lord only forbade you this tree lest you become angels or become of the immortals. And he swore to them: I am to you a sincere adviser. So he brought them down by delusion. When they tasted the tree their nakedness appeared to them and they began to fasten on themselves leaves of the garden. Their Lord called them: did I not forbid you that tree and say to you that Satan is a clear enemy to you? They said: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us we will be of the losers. He said: get down, some of you enemies to others. For you in the earth a settlement and enjoyment for a time. He said: in it you will live and in it you will die and from it you will be brought out.
2. Structural Analysis

1–10: Book, follow, destroyed towns, questioning of recipients and messengers, scales. 11–18: Iblīs refuses, fire-over-clay, respite, ambush on the path, Jahannam filled. 19–25: garden command, whisper, oath, tasting, nakedness, leaf-covering, confession, descent to earth.
3. Verse-by-Verse Investigation
7:1–10 Book; towns; scales

Four isolated letters. Book sent down; no constriction in the breast; warn and remind. Follow what was sent down; do not follow awliyāʾ besides Him. Towns destroyed at night or at noon-nap; their only cry: we were ẓālimīn. Recipients and messengers both questioned. Weighing is the truth. Heavy scales: mufliḥūn. Light scales: lost their souls. Established in the earth with livelihoods; little thanks.
2:34 already walked the prostration-exception. This surah retells it at full length and adds the garden-whisper that 2:35–36 only sketched.
7:11–18 Iblis: fire not clay; ambush on the path

Created you, then fashioned you, then the angels were told to prostrate to Adam. Iblīs was not of the prostrators. Reason given: I am better; fire vs clay. Get down; pride not allowed here. Respite to the raising. Because You sent me astray I will sit on Your straight path and come from four sides; most will not be thankful. Get out, disgraced, banished; Jahannam filled with you and whoever follows.
Aghwaytanī — ‘You have sent me astray’ / ‘let me go astray’ — is a split locus (§5). The four-direction ambush is this telling’s extra. 2:34 had no fire-clay speech.
7:19–25 the tree, the oath, the leaves, the confession

Adam and his wife: dwell, eat where you will, do not approach this tree. Satan whispers to show them what was hidden of their sawʾa. Motive he names: lest you become angels or immortals. He swears: I am a sincere adviser. He brought them down by ghurūr. They tasted; nakedness appeared; they fastened garden leaves. Called: did I not forbid you and say Satan is an enemy? They: our Lord, we wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive and have mercy we are losers. Get down, enemies to one another; settlement and enjoyment for a time. In it you live, in it you die, from it you are brought out.

No serpent. No named tree of knowledge. No ‘you will be like God.’ The offered goods are malakayn or khālidīn. Both eat; both confess; no ‘she gave to her husband’ sequence. Forgiveness is asked; 2:37 already had words received. Descent is to earth as settlement, not a cherub-and-sword scene.
4. Linguistic / Key-Lemma Notes

ḥaraj — constriction. mawāzīn — scales. sajada / sājidīn. ṭīn vs nār. aghwaytanī. ṣirāṭaka l-mustaqīm. sawʾāt — nakedness/shame. malakayn / khālidīn. ghurūr — delusion. waraq al-janna — garden leaves. iblis as proper name already in 2:34.
5. Translation Analysis (core five on split loci)
Locus
Split among core five
Return to Arabic
7:12 fire vs clay
SI: fire / clay. Haleem: fire / clay. Pickthall: fire / mud. Arberry: fire / clay.
min nar / min tin. Pickthall's mud is still tin. No split that changes the hierarchy-claim.
7:16 aghwaytani
SI: because You have put me in error. Haleem: You have condemned me. Pickthall: because Thou hast sent me astray. Arberry: for Thy perverting me.
aghwaytani from gh-w-y. Subject is God in Iblis's mouth. Gloss range: sent astray / perverted / condemned. Level 1: Iblis assigns the ghawayah to God as the reason for the ambush.
7:20 malakayn or khalidin
SI: angels or immortals. Haleem: angels or of the immortal. Pickthall: angels or of the immortals. Arberry: angels or such as dwell forever.
malakayn (dual angels) / khalidin. Not 'like God' (Gen 3:5 ke'lohim). Dual angels is this wording.
7:22 saw'atuhuma
SI: their private parts. Haleem: their nakedness. Pickthall: their shame. Arberry: their shameful parts.
saw'a = shame / nakedness / pudenda. All four land in the same field. Leaves of the garden fastened as cover.
Yusuf Ali 7:20 line only: 'your Lord only forbade you this tree, lest ye should become angels or such beings as live for ever.' Confirms angels-or-immortals, not like-God.
6. Theological Findings

Pride ranked over clay is the refusal. Respite is granted. The garden-ban is a tree plus an enemy-warning. The fall is shared tasting plus shared confession. Earth is settlement and death-place and raising-place. Scales will weigh.
7. Internal Quran Cross-References

2:30–39 khalifa, prostration, garden, words received, descent. 15:28–43 and 38:71–85 parked (fire-clay again, more Iblis speech). 20:115–123 parked (forgetfulness, no resolve). 7:26–27 will continue children-of-Adam clothing.
8. Biblical Cross-References

Gen 2–3: garden, tree-ban, serpent, eyes opened, fig leaves, blame-shift, expulsion, cherubim and sword. No Iblīs in Genesis. Serpent is the beast, later read as Satan in Rev 12:9. Job’s Satan is a different office.
9. Agreement / Difference Analysis
QB-0162 PARTIAL AGREEMENT: a first pair in a garden, a forbidden tree, a deceiver, opened awareness of nakedness, leaf-cover, expulsion to a hard earth.

QB-0163 CONTRAST: no serpent; no tree-of-knowledge name; no ‘like God’; both confess and ask mercy (no Adam-blames-Eve); Iblīs is a fire-creature who refused a prostration, not a walking beast; respite until the raising; four-sided ambush on the ṣirāṭ.
Living snapshot. 15 and 20 will rebuild the Adam dossier, not this table’s last word.
10–12. Context, parallels, QRQ
Meccan warning-surah opening. QRQ-0008 garden/fall. QRQ-0001 pride as first refusal. No datable public event.

17–20. Dictionary, dossiers, provenance

Lemmas: haraj, mawazin, tin/nar, aghwaya, saw'a, ghurur. Adam dossier: full garden-whisper added to 2:35–37. God: questions messengers and people; scales; grants respite; fills Jahannam. Level 1 text. Iblis fire-origin is asserted here as his claim.
21. Executive Checkpoint Summary
Al-Aʿrāf opens with a Book and scales, then retells Adam at full length: Iblīs will not bow to clay; the pair will not keep the tree; both ask mercy; earth is the timed settlement.

packets.title: S007 Al-Araf CP02 vv026-053
paragraphs: S007 — AL-AʿRĀF — CP02
Unit: 7:26–53 (28 verses)
Translations: Arabic primary. Core five on split loci.
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

O children of Adam, We have sent down on you a garment to cover your nakedness and plumage; the garment of taqwā is better. That is of God’s signs, that they may remember. O children of Adam, do not let Satan seduce you as he brought your two parents out of the garden, stripping them of their garment to show them their nakedness. He and his tribe see you from where you do not see them. We have made the satans allies of those who do not believe. When they do an indecency they say we found our fathers upon it and God commanded us to it. Say: God does not command indecency. Do you say about God what you do not know? Say: my Lord commands justice. Set your faces at every mosque and call Him, making the dīn sincerely His. As He originated you, you will return. A party He guided; a party, error was justified against them. They took satans as allies besides God and they think they are guided. O children of Adam, take your adornment at every mosque. Eat and drink and do not waste; He does not love the wasters. Say: who has forbidden the adornment God has brought out for His servants and the good things of provision? Say: they are for those who believe in the life of this world, exclusive on the Day of Rising. Thus We set out the signs for a people who know. Say: my Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is outward of them and what is inward, and sin, and aggression without right, and that you associate with God that for which He sent down no authority, and that you say about God what you do not know.

Every community has a term. When their term comes they cannot delay it an hour or advance it. O children of Adam, if messengers come to you from among you recounting My signs, whoever fears and puts right — no fear on them and they shall not grieve. Those who deny Our signs and grow proud against them — companions of the Fire, they abide. Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against God or denies His signs? Those, their portion of the Book reaches them until, when Our messengers come to them to take them, they say: where is what you used to call besides God? They say: they have gone from us. They witness against themselves that they were disbelievers. He says: enter among communities of jinn and humans that have passed before you into the Fire. Whenever a community enters it curses its sister. When they have all caught up, the last of them says of the first: our Lord, these led us astray; give them a double punishment of the Fire. He says: for each is double, but you do not know. The first of them says to the last: you have no advantage over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn.

Those who deny Our signs and grow proud against them — the gates of heaven will not be opened for them and they will not enter the garden until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Thus We repay the criminals. Their bed is Jahannam and from above them coverings. Thus We repay the ẓālimīn. Those who believe and do ṣāliḥāt — We do not charge a soul except its capacity — they are companions of the garden, abiding. We will strip what is in their breasts of rancor; rivers under them; they say praise to God who guided us to this; we would not have been guided if God had not guided us; the messengers of our Lord came with the truth. They are called: that is the garden you are given as heirs for what you used to do. The companions of the garden call the companions of the Fire: we have found what our Lord promised us true; have you found what your Lord promised you true? They say: yes. Then an announcer announces between them: the curse of God is on the ẓālimīn — who bar from God’s path and seek to make it crooked and deny the hereafter. Between them is a ḥijāb. On the aʿrāf are men who recognize each by their mark. They call the companions of the garden: peace upon you. They have not entered it though they hope. When their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire they say: our Lord, do not place us with the unjust people. The companions of the aʿrāf call men they recognize by their mark: your gathering has not availed you, nor what you used to grow proud of. Are these the ones you swore God would not reach with mercy? Enter the garden; no fear on you, you will not grieve. The companions of the Fire call the companions of the garden: pour on us some water or some of what God has provided you. They say: God has forbidden them to the disbelievers — who took their dīn as diversion and play and whom the life of this world deceived. Today We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs and as they used to deny Our signs. We have brought them a Book which We have detailed with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe. Are they waiting except for its taʾwīl? The day its taʾwīl comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: the messengers of our Lord came with the truth; have we any intercessors to intercede for us, or can we be returned to do other than what we used to do? They have lost their souls and what they invented has gone from them.
2. Structural Analysis

26–33 children of Adam: garment, do not be seduced, God does not command fahisha, adornment at the mosque, eat and do not waste, what is actually forbidden. 34–41 term of every ummah; messengers; Fire-communities curse each other. 42–45 garden and Fire call across. 46–49 the ḥijāb and the men on the aʿrāf. 50–53 water refused; Book detailed; waiting for its taʾwīl.
3. Investigation
7:26–33 garment of taqwa; God does not command indecency

Clothing sent down to cover sawʾāt, plus rīsh (plumage / finery). The garment of taqwā is better. Satan stripped the two parents. He and his tribe see you from where you do not see them. Satans allied to unbelievers. When they do fahisha: we found our fathers, and God commanded it. God does not command fahisha. My Lord commands justice. Adornment at every mosque. Eat and drink; do not waste. Who forbade the adornment God brought out? For believers in this world, exclusive on the Rising. Forbidden only: fahisha outward and inward, ithm, baghy without right, shirk with no authority, saying about God what you do not know.
Fathers-plus-God-commanded-it is the same excuse-pattern as 5:104 / 6:148. The garment-file answers 7:22’s leaves: God now sends cover.
7:34–41 every ummah a term; communities in the Fire curse their sisters

A term that cannot be moved an hour. Messengers from among you; who fears and puts right: no fear, no grief. Deniers-and-proud: Fire, abiding. Invented lie or denied signs: their Book-portion reaches them until the death-messengers; the associates are gone. Enter among past communities of jinn and humans. Each entering community curses its sister. Last asks double for the first; each already has double. First: you have no advantage.
7:42–53 garden and Fire; the Heights; ta'wil of the Book

Believers-and-ṣāliḥ, capacity not exceeded: garden. Rancor stripped from breasts. Messengers came with the truth. Garden calls Fire: we found the promise true — have you? Yes. Announcer: curse on those who bar the path. Between them a ḥijāb. On the aʿrāf men who know each by their mark. They greet the garden; they have not entered though they hope. They ask not to be placed with the unjust. They mock the proud: are these the ones you swore mercy would not reach? Enter the garden. Fire asks for water or provision; refused. God has forbidden them to the disbelievers who took dīn as play. Today We forget them as they forgot this meeting. A Book detailed with knowledge. Are they waiting except its taʾwīl? The day it comes, the forgetters want intercessors or a return.

Who the men on the aʿrāf are is argued in tafsir (people of equal scale, honored watchers, prophets). Level 1: men on a height between garden and Fire, who recognize marks, who have not yet entered, who hope, who can address both sides. Do not pick a school.
4. Lemmas
libās / rīsh / libās al-taqwā. sawʾāt. qawm / ummah / ajal. samm al-khiyāṭ (eye of the needle). ghill (rancor). ḥijāb. aʿrāf. sīmā (mark). taʾwīl.
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Locus
Split among core five
Return to Arabic
7:26 rish / libas al-taqwa

SI: clothing to conceal private parts and as adornment; clothing of righteousness is best. Haleem: garments to cover nakedness and as adornment; garment of mindfulness is best. Pickthall: raiment to conceal shame, and splendid vesture; raiment of restraint from evil. Arberry: garment to cover your shame, and plumage; garment of godfearing is better.
libasan yuwwari saw'atikum wa-rishan. rish = plumage / finery / adornment. libas al-taqwa is the better garment. SI's 'righteousness' is a gloss of taqwa.
7:40 hatta yalija al-jamalu fi sammi l-khiyat
SI: until a camel enters into the eye of a needle. Haleem / Pickthall / Arberry: camel / needle.
al-jamal / samm al-khiyat. Same image as Mark 10:25 / Matt 19:24 / Luke 18:25. Do not spend variant 'thick rope' readings as if they were this Arabic.
7:46 ala l-a'raf rijal
SI: on [its] elevations are men. Haleem: on the heights. Pickthall: on the Heights. Arberry: on the Battlements.
a'raf = heights / elevations / battlements. The surah's name. Identity of the rijal is not in the verse.
7:53 ta'wilahu
SI: its fulfillment / interpretation. Haleem: its unfolding. Pickthall: the fulfilment thereof. Arberry: its interpretation.
ta'wil = outcome / interpretation / unfolding. The day the Book's ta'wil comes, late regret.
Yusuf Ali 7:40 line only: 'until the camel can pass through the eye of the needle.' Same image.
6. Theological Findings

Cover is given after the fall-scene. God does not command fahisha; fathers are not a warrant. Every ummah has a moved-not term. Garden and Fire already converse. A third place — the Heights — holds men who recognize and hope. The Book has a taʾwīl that will arrive.
7. Internal cross-references
7:22 leaves; 6:151 fahisha outward/inward; 5:104 fathers; 2:286 capacity; 7:8–9 scales. 7:54 six days next, not this packet.
8. Biblical cross-references

Gen 3:21 skins as cover after leaves — cousin to 7:26 sent-down garment. Mark 10:25 camel through a needle. Luke 16:19–31 rich man asking for water across a gulf — POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of the call-across, not identity with the aʿrāf.
9. Agreement / Difference
QB-0169 PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Gen 3:21 God-given cover after shame. Quran adds the better garment of taqwā and a warning that Satan still strips.
QB-0170 POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of camel-needle with the synoptic saying; same impossibility-image, different frame (pride against signs vs rich man and kingdom).
QB-0171 POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of a gulf-call (Luke 16) with garden/Fire speech; the aʿrāf men have no Lukan name.
10–12. Context, QRQ
Meccan. Namesake of the surah arrives. QRQ-0008 afterlife geography. QRQ-0007: God does not command fahisha; adornment not forbidden.

Lemmas: libas, rish, a'raf, ta'wil, samm al-khiyat. God: does not command fahisha; forgets those who forgot the meeting. Level 1: a'raf identity unsolved.

After the fall, cover is sent down. The Heights get their men. The Book’s taʾwīl is still ahead of those who forgot it.

packets.title: S007 Al-Araf CP03 vv054-064
paragraphs: S007 — AL-AʿRĀF — CP03
Unit: 7:54–64 (11 verses)
Translations: Arabic primary. Core five on split loci.
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

Your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then istawā ʿalā l-ʿarsh. He covers the night with the day, which pursues it urgently; the sun and the moon and the stars are musakhkharāt by His command. His is the creation and the command. Blessed is God, Lord of the worlds. Call your Lord in humility and in secret. He does not love the aggressors. Do not work corruption in the earth after it has been set right. Call Him in fear and hope. God’s mercy is near the good-doers. He is the one who sends the winds as good news before His mercy, until when they bear a heavy cloud We drive it to a dead land and send down by it water and bring out by it all the fruits. Thus We bring out the dead; perhaps you will remember. The good land’s plant comes out by its Lord’s leave; what is bad comes out scantily. Thus We turn the signs for a people who are thankful.

We sent Noah to his people. He said: O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him. I fear for you the punishment of a great day. The notables of his people said: we see you in clear error. He said: O my people, there is no error in me; I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds. I deliver to you the messages of my Lord and I advise you, and I know from God what you do not know. Or do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord upon a man from among you, that he may warn you and that you may fear and that you may receive mercy? They denied him, so We delivered him and those with him in the ship, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. They were a blind people.
2. Structural Analysis

54–58: six-day creation, throne, lamps under command, call in secret, no corruption after iṣlāḥ, winds-cloud-rain as a raising-sign. 59–64: first messenger-panel of the surah — Noah, notables, ship, drowning.
3. Investigation
7:54 six days then istawa — now walked
Khalaqa l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa fī sittati ayyām thumma stawā ʿalā l-ʿarsh. Night covered by day in urgent pursuit. Sun, moon, stars subjected by His command. His is the creation and the amr. Tabāraka.

This is the first six-day sentence walked in order. It is not Genesis 1’s numbered week. No evening-and-morning. No ‘God saw that it was good.’ No seventh-day rest. After the six comes istawā on the throne — a session, not a sabbath. Lamps are musakhkharāt, not day-4 rulers installed after light.

Still parked: 10:3; 11:7 (throne on water); 25:59; 32:4; 41:9–12 two-four-two; 50:38 no weariness; 57:4. The Genesis 1 snapshot should be rebuilt to move 7:54 off the parking list. 50:38 remains the weariness-contrast.
7:55–58 call Him; do not corrupt; rain raises the dead-land

Call in humility and secret. He does not love aggressors. Do not work fasād after the earth was set right. Call in fear and hope; mercy is near the good-doers. Winds as good news before His mercy; heavy cloud; water on a dead land; all fruits. Thus the dead are brought out. Good land yields by leave; bad land scantily.

Worship God; you have no god other than Him. I fear a great day’s punishment. Notables: you are in clear error. I am a messenger; I deliver; I advise; I know from God what you do not. Do you wonder that a reminder came on a man from among you? They denied. He and those with him delivered in the ship. Deniers drowned. They were a blind people.
No ark-dimensions. No raven/dove. No rainbow covenant. No drunkenness after. A messenger-plus-ship-plus-drowning panel. 11:25–49 and 23:23–30 and 71 parked for the longer Noah files.
4. Lemmas
sittati ayyām. istawā ʿalā l-ʿarsh. musakhkharāt. amr. ʿarsh. fasād / aṣlaḥa. nashr al-mawtā via rain. malaʾ (notables). fulk (ship).
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Locus
Split among core five
Return to Arabic
7:54 sittati ayyam
SI: six days. Haleem: six Days. Pickthall: six Days. Arberry: six days.
sittati ayyam. Capital D in Haleem/Pickthall does not change the count. No 'periods' or 'aeons' in the four. Do not import that gloss here.
7:54 thumma stawa 'ala l-'arsh
SI: established Himself above the Throne. Haleem: established Himself on the throne. Pickthall: mounted He the Throne. Arberry: sat Himself upon the Throne.
istawa 'ala. Range: established / mounted / sat. Bi-la kayf is tafsir. Level 1 is the verb plus the throne after the six days.
7:54 al-khalqu wa-l-amr
SI: creation and command. Haleem: creation and command. Pickthall: creation and commandment. Arberry: creation and the command.
Shared. Creation and amr both His.
7:64 al-fulk
SI: ship. Haleem: Ark. Pickthall: ship. Arberry: ship.
fulk = ship. Haleem's Ark is a biblical capitalization, not a second Arabic word.
Yusuf Ali 7:54 line only: 'created the heavens and the earth in six days, and is firmly established on the throne.' Same count; 'firmly established' is his istawa.
6. Theological Findings

Six days plus throne-session is now on the walked page. Lamps serve. Mercy near the good-doers. Rain is a raising-parable. Noah’s message is tawḥīd plus a feared day; the notables call it error; the ship saves a group; the rest drown.
7. Internal cross-references
6:73 Be and trumpet; 6:96–97 lamps as reckoning. 10:71–73; 11:25–49; 23:23–30; 26:105–122; 71 whole — parked Noah. 50:38 parked no-weariness.
8. Biblical cross-references
Gen 1:1–2:3 six days plus rest. Exod 31:17 rest and refreshment. Gen 6–9 Noah, ark, flood, covenant. 1 Pet 3:20 eight souls.
9. Agreement / Difference

QB-0172 PARTIAL AGREEMENT on a six-unit creation of heaven and earth. CONTRAST of the seventh slot: Genesis rests and blesses the day; 7:54 sessions on the throne. CONTRAST of form: no numbered evenings. Rebuild Comparison_Genesis_Chapter_1: 7:54 is no longer parked.
QB-0173 PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Gen 6–9: a warner, a ship, drowning of deniers. CONTRAST: no dimensions, animals-two-by-two, raven, dove, altar, rainbow, or vineyard in this panel.
10–12. Context, QRQ
Meccan. First of the destroyed-people cycle in this surah. QRQ-0001 creation-and-command. QRQ-0004 Noah as rasūl from among them.

QDISC-0312

QDISC-0313

QDISC-0314

Six days vs Gen 1 week; throne-session vs sabbath-rest

17–20. Dictionary, dossiers, provenance

packets.title: S007 Al-Araf CP04 vv065-093
paragraphs: S007 — AL-AʿRĀF — CP04
Unit: 7:65–93 (29 verses)
Translations: Arabic primary. Core five on split loci.
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

To ʿĀd, their brother Hūd: worship God; you have no god other than Him; will you not fear? The disbelieving notables: we see you in foolishness and think you of the liars. He: no foolishness; I am a messenger; I deliver; I am a trustworthy adviser. Do you wonder that a reminder came on a man from among you? Remember He made you successors after Noah’s people and increased you in stature. Remember God’s bounties. They: have you come that we should worship God alone and leave what our fathers worshipped? Bring what you promise if you are truthful. He: filth and wrath from your Lord have fallen on you. Do you dispute with me about names you and your fathers named, for which God sent down no authority? Wait; I am with you waiting. We saved him and those with him by mercy. We cut off the last of those who denied Our signs and were not believers.

To Thamūd, their brother Ṣāliḥ: worship God; you have no god other than Him. A bayyina has come. This is the she-camel of God, a sign for you. Leave her to eat in God’s land; do not touch her with harm, lest a painful punishment take you. Remember He made you successors after ʿĀd, settled you in the land; you take palaces from its plains and carve homes from the mountains. Remember His bounties; do not act wickedly in the earth corrupting. The proud notables to those who believed among the weak: do you know that Ṣāliḥ is sent from his Lord? They: we believe in what he was sent with. Those who grew proud: we disbelieve in what you believe. They hamstrung the she-camel, insolently defied their Lord’s command, and said: O Ṣāliḥ, bring what you promise if you are a messenger. The earthquake took them and they lay in their home fallen. He turned from them: O my people, I delivered to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not love advisers.

Lot when he said to his people: do you commit the indecency no one in the worlds preceded you in? You approach men with desire instead of women. You are a people exceeding. His people’s answer was only: expel them from your town; they are people who keep themselves pure. We saved him and his family except his wife; she was of those who stayed behind. We rained on them a rain. See how the criminals ended.

To Midian, their brother Shuʿayb: worship God; you have no god other than Him. A bayyina has come. Give the measure and the weight; do not deprive people of their things; do not work corruption in the earth after it was set right. That is better for you if you are believers. Do not sit on every path threatening and barring from God’s path those who believe in Him, seeking to make it crooked. Remember when you were few and He increased you. See how the corrupters ended. If a party of you believed in what I was sent with and a party did not, be patient until God judges between us; He is the best of judges. The proud notables: we will expel you, O Shuʿayb, and those who believe with you from our town, or you shall return to our millah. He: even if we are unwilling? We would have invented a lie against God if we returned to your millah after God delivered us from it. It is not for us to return to it unless God our Lord wills. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. On God we rely. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth; You are the best of deciders. The disbelieving notables: if you follow Shuʿayb you will be losers. The earthquake took them; they lay in their home fallen. Those who denied Shuʿayb — it was as if they had never flourished there. Those who denied Shuʿayb were the losers. He turned from them: O my people, I delivered to you the messages of my Lord and advised you. How should I grieve for a disbelieving people?
2. Structural Analysis

Four brother-messenger panels after Noah, same spine: tawḥīd, notables, a sign or a social crime, save-and-destroy. Hūd: stature and successors, names without authority. Ṣāliḥ: she-camel, palaces and carved mountains, hamstring, earthquake. Lot: fahisha with men, expulsion of the purifiers, wife excepted, rain. Shuʿayb: measure and weight, barring the path, expel-or-return-to-our-millah, earthquake.
3. Investigation
7:65–72 Hud and Ad

Brother to his people. Same opening as Noah. Notables: foolishness and lies. He: trustworthy adviser. Successors after Noah’s people; increased stature. They: we should leave our fathers’ gods? Bring the promise. Names you named, no authority sent down. Saved by mercy; last of the deniers cut off.
7:73–79 Salih and Thamud

She-camel of God as a sign: leave her to eat; do not harm her. Successors after ʿĀd; palaces on plains; homes carved in mountains. Proud notables test the weak believers; then they hamstring the camel and dare the promise. Earthquake. He leaves: I delivered; you do not love advisers.

Fahisha no one in the worlds preceded. Approach men with desire instead of women. Answer: expel them; they keep themselves pure. Saved him and his family except his wife, who stayed behind. A rain. See the end of the criminals.

No visitors at the door in this panel. No daughters offered. No pillar of salt named — only ‘she stayed behind.’ Living snapshot vs Gen 19. 11:77–83 and 15:61–77 and 26:160–175 parked for the fuller Lot files.
7:85–93 Shuayb and Midian

Measure and weight; do not deprive people; no fasād after iṣlāḥ. Do not sit on every road threatening and barring believers. Few made many. Split community: wait for God’s judgment. Notables: expel or return to our millah. Return after God delivered us would be a lie against God unless He wills. Earthquake. As if they had never flourished. How should I grieve for a disbelieving people?
4. Lemmas
akhāhum (their brother). mala'. nāqat Allāh. ʿaqarū (hamstrung). rajfa (earthquake). jāthimīn (fallen prone). fāḥisha. al-ghābirīn (those who stayed behind). kayl / mīzān. millah.
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Locus
Split among core five
Return to Arabic
7:73 naqat Allah
SI: she-camel of Allah [sent] as a sign. Haleem: God's camel, a sign. Pickthall: she-camel of Allah, a token. Arberry: She-camel of God, to be a sign.
naqat Allah lakum ayatan. Leave her to eat; do not touch with harm. Species and ownership-metaphor are the Arabic; 'sent' is SI's bracket.
7:81 ta'tuna l-rijala shahwatan min duni l-nisa'
SI: you approach men with desire, instead of women. Haleem: you lust after men rather than women. Pickthall: lust with men instead of women. Arberry: you approach men lustfully instead of women.
Shared. shahwa / lust / desire. min duni l-nisa' = instead of / apart from women.
7:83 illa mra'atahu kanat mina l-ghabirin

SI: except his wife; she was of those who remained. Haleem: except his wife, who stayed behind. Pickthall: except his wife, who was of those who stayed behind. Arberry: except his wife; she was one of those that tarried.
al-ghabirin = those who remained / tarried / stayed behind. No salt-pillar in this verse.
7:88 aw la-ta'udunna fi millatina
SI: or you shall return to our religion. Haleem: or you will return to our religion. Pickthall: or ye return to our religion. Arberry: or you will return to our creed.
millah = creed / religion / community-way. Same word as Abraham's millah in 6:161.
Yusuf Ali 7:83 line only: 'except his wife; she was of those who lagged behind.' Same as ghabirin.
6. Theological Findings

The destroyed-people cycle runs on one hinge: worship God alone. Extra crimes differ: inherited names (ʿĀd), harming a sign-animal and pride in stone houses (Thamūd), same-sex fahisha (Lot’s people), crooked weights and road-blocking (Midian). Save-by-mercy and cut-off / earthquake / rain are the three ends. A wife can fail the save. Return to a millah after deliverance would be a lie against God.
7. Internal cross-references
26 and 11 longer panels parked. 11:69–83 Lot visitors parked. 15:80–84 Ḥijr/Thamūd parked. 26:176–191 Shuʿayb parked.
8. Biblical cross-references

Gen 19 Sodom: men of the city, Lot’s visitors, daughters offered, wife looks back, sulfur. No biblical Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, or Shuʿayb. Amos 1:1 / earthquake as judgment is loose. Honest weights: Lev 19:35–36; Deut 25:13–16; Prov 11:1.
9. Agreement / Difference

QB-0174 PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Gen 19 on a condemned fahisha, a saved household minus the wife, a rain of destruction. CONTRAST: no angel-guests, no door-scene, no daughters offered, no looking-back/salt in this panel.
QB-0175 PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Torah honest-weights law. Shuʿayb’s millah-or-expel is this text’s.
Hūd / Ṣāliḥ / she-camel have no Genesis counterpart. Record as Quran-only cycle-members.
10–12. Context, QRQ
Meccan destroyed-nations cycle. QRQ-0004 rasūl is their brother. QRQ-0007 weights and no fasād.

packets.title: S007 Al-Araf CP05 vv094-126
paragraphs: S007 — AL-AʿRĀF — CP05
Unit: 7:94–126 (33 verses)
Translations: Arabic primary. Core five on split loci.
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

We did not send a prophet to a town except We seized its people with misery and hardship that they might humble themselves. Then We gave good in place of the evil until they multiplied and said: hardship and ease touched our fathers. Then We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive. If the people of the towns had believed and feared, We would have opened on them blessings from heaven and earth. But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn. Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our violence will not come at night while they sleep? Or that it will not come in daylight while they play? Do they feel secure from God’s plan? None feels secure from God’s plan except the losing people. Has it not guided those who inherit the earth after its people that if We will We can strike them for their sins and seal their hearts so they do not hear? Those towns: We recount to you some of their news. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. They were not to believe in what they had denied before. Thus God seals the hearts of the disbelievers. We did not find most of them in covenant. We found most of them defiantly disobedient.

Then We sent after them Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his notables. They were unjust to them. See the end of the corrupters. Moses said: O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds. It is right that I say about God only the truth. I have come to you with a proof from your Lord, so send with me the Children of Israel. He said: if you have come with a sign, bring it if you are truthful. He threw his staff and it was a serpent, manifest. He drew his hand and it was white to the onlookers. The notables of Pharaoh’s people: this is a knowing magician who wants to expel you from your land. What do you command? They: delay him and his brother and send gatherers in the cities to bring you every knowing magician. The magicians came to Pharaoh. They: is there a reward for us if we prevail? He: yes, and you will be of those brought near. They: O Moses, throw or we throw. He: throw. When they threw they bewitched the people’s eyes and struck them with terror and brought a great magic. We revealed to Moses: throw your staff. It swallowed what they falsified. The truth came to pass and what they did was vain. They were defeated there and turned back small. The magicians were flung down prostrating. They said: we believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron. Pharaoh: you believed in him before I gave you leave. This is a plot you plotted in the city to expel its people from it. You will know. I will cut your hands and feet on opposite sides then I will crucify you all. They: we are turned to our Lord. You take vengeance on us only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour on us patience and take us as muslims.
2. Structural Analysis

94–102: how towns are seized — hardship then ease then sudden take; security is folly; hearts sealed after prior denial. 103–108: Moses to Pharaoh; staff-serpent; white hand. 109–126: magicians summoned, paid, throw first, swallowed, prostrate, believe, threatened with opposite-side cutting and crucifixion, ask for patience and to die muslim.
3. Investigation
7:94–102 the seizure-pattern

Every town that received a prophet was first seized with baʾsāʾ and ḍarrāʾ that they might humble themselves. Then ease until they said our fathers had both. Then sudden seizure. Blessings from heaven and earth were on offer for īmān and taqwā. Night-violence and day-violence. No one feels secure from God’s plan except losers. Heirs of the earth can still be struck and sealed. Messengers came with proofs; they would not believe what they had already denied. Most not found in ʿahd. Most fāsiqīn.
7:103–108 staff and hand

Moses sent after those towns to Pharaoh and his malaʾ. Unjust to the signs. I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds. I say about God only the truth. Proof from your Lord: send with me the Children of Israel. If you have a sign, bring it. Staff becomes a thuʿbān, manifest. Hand comes out white to the onlookers.
2:49–50 already walked a short drowning. This is the first long Moses–Pharaoh panel. No burning bush in this block. No ‘I AM’ name.
7:109–126 magicians believe and are threatened with crucifixion

Notables: a knowing magician who will expel you. Delay him and Aaron; gather every knowing magician. Magicians ask a wage; they will be brought near. They throw first; eyes bewitched; great magic. Moses throws; staff swallows what they falsified. Truth stands; their work vain; they turn small. Magicians flung down sajidīn. We believe in the Lord of the worlds, Lord of Moses and Aaron. Pharaoh: you believed before my leave; this is a city-plot. Hands and feet on opposite sides, then crucifixion of all. They: we are turned to our Lord. You take vengeance only because we believed. Pour patience; take us as muslims.
Aaron is named here as co-referent of the Lord, not yet as speaker. Crucifixion (uṣallibannakum) is Pharaoh’s threat against the magicians, not a Jesus-file.
4. Lemmas
ba'sa' / darra'. makr Allah. thu'ban mubin. yad bayda'. sahara / sahir 'alim. talaqqa / alqā. ʿaks / min khilaf (opposite sides). usallibannakum. muslimin as dying-state.
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Locus
Split among core five
Return to Arabic
7:107 thu'ban mubin
SI: serpent, manifest. Haleem: snake, clear. Pickthall: serpent manifest. Arberry: serpent manifest.
thu'ban not hayya (20:20 parked). Manifest / clear = mubin.
7:108 yadahu fa-idha hiya bayda'u lil-nazirin
SI: white [with radiance] for the observers. Haleem: white to the onlookers. Pickthall: white for the beholders. Arberry: white to the beholders.
bayda' = white. SI's '[with radiance]' is a gloss. Not 'leprous' as some Exod 4:6 readings.
7:124 usallibannakum ajma'in
SI: crucify you all. Haleem: crucify you all. Pickthall: crucify you every one. Arberry: crucify you all together.
s-l-b. Same root later used in 4:157's crucifixion file. Here it is Pharaoh's judicial threat.
7:126 tawaffana muslimin
SI: cause us to die as Muslims. Haleem: take our souls in submission to You. Pickthall: make us die as men who have surrendered. Arberry: take us to Thee as Muslims.
muslimin = those who submit / have surrendered. Haleem unpacks; SI/Arberry keep the later communal noun.
Yusuf Ali 7:107 line only: 'it was a serpent, plain for all to see.' Same as mubin.
6. Theological Findings

Towns are trained by hardship then ease then a sudden take. Prior denial can lock later proof out. Moses’ first two signs are staff and hand. Court-magic is allowed to run, then swallowed. The magicians’ sajda is immediate confession of the Lord of Moses and Aaron. Pharaoh hears a coup. They ask to be taken muslim.
7. Internal cross-references
2:49–50 drowning already walked. 20, 26, 28, 40, 43 parked Moses panels. 26:31–51 closest twin of this magician-scene.
8. Biblical cross-references

Exod 3 bush (absent here). Exod 4:3–7 staff-snake and leprous/restored hand. Exod 7:8–13 staff becomes tannin; Egyptian magicians do the same; Aaron’s staff swallows theirs. Exod 7:11 Jannes-and-Jambres are later names (2 Tim 3:8), not Exodus’s.
9. Agreement / Difference
QB-0179 PARTIAL AGREEMENT: Moses before Pharaoh with staff-serpent and a changed hand; court magicians compete; the staff swallows their work.

QB-0180 CONTRAST: Exodus has Aaron throw in 7:10; this panel Moses throws. Exodus magicians copy the sign and are not said to convert. Here they fall sajid and confess. Pharaoh’s opposite-side cutting and crucifixion are this telling’s. No bush, no ten-plague list yet.

packets.title: S007 Al-Araf CP06 vv127-141
paragraphs: S007 — AL-AʿRĀF — CP06
Unit: 7:127–141 (15 verses)
Translations: Arabic primary. Core five on split loci.
Date: 12 September 2026
1. Overview

The notables of Pharaoh’s people: will you leave Moses and his people to work corruption in the land and leave you and your gods? He: we will slay their sons and spare their women; we are subjugators over them. Moses to his people: seek help from God and be patient. The earth is God’s; He bequeaths it to whom He wills of His servants. The aftermath is for the God-fearing. They: we were harmed before you came to us and after you came. He: perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and look how you act.

We seized Pharaoh’s house with years of drought and a deficit of fruits, that they might remember. When good came they said this is ours. When evil hit them they took Moses and those with him as an omen. Their omen is only with God, but most of them do not know. They: whatever sign you bring to bewitch us, we will not believe you. So We sent on them the ṭūfān, the locusts, the qummal, the frogs, and the blood — distinct signs. They grew proud and were a criminal people. When the wrath fell on them they said: O Moses, call your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you. If you remove the wrath from us we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you. When We removed the wrath from them to a term they were to reach, they broke it. So We took vengeance on them and drowned them in the yamm because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them. We made the people who had been weakened inherit the eastern parts of the land and its western parts, which We had blessed. The good word of your Lord was fulfilled on the Children of Israel for their patience. We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been making and what they had been erecting. We brought the Children of Israel across the sea. They came on a people clinging to idols of theirs. They: O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods. He: you are a people ignorant. These — what they are in is ruined, and vain is what they have been doing. He: shall I seek for you a god other than God, when He has favored you over the worlds? When We saved you from Pharaoh’s house, who were afflicting you with evil punishment, slaying your sons and sparing your women. In that was a great trial from your Lord.
2. Structural Analysis

127–129: notables push son-killing again; Moses answers with patience and succession. 130–135: drought-omen; five-sign list; promise-and-breach. 136–137: drowning; inheritance of blessed land-parts; Pharaoh’s works destroyed. 138–141: crossing; request for an idol like the people they met; reminder of the trial they just left.
3. Investigation
7:127–129 slay the sons again; the earth is God's

Same policy as 2:49, restated as Pharaoh’s answer to his notables. Moses does not counter with a plague-threat here. He names the earth as God’s to bequeath, and the ʿāqiba as the muttaqīn’s. The people say harm came before and after he arrived. He: perhaps destruction of the enemy and succession — then look how you act. Succession is conditional in that last clause.
7:130–135 drought, omen, five signs, broken promise

Years (sinīn) and deficit of fruits. Good: this is ours. Evil: omen on Moses. Omen is with God. Whatever sign you bring to bewitch us we will not believe — a pre-commitment to unbelief. Then five: ṭūfān, jarād, qummal, ḍafādiʿ, dam — signs set out (āyāt mufaṣṣalāt). Wrath falls; they bargain: call your Lord by what He covenanted with you; we will believe and send Israel. Wrath lifted to a term; they break it.
This is the first walked plague-list. It is five named blows plus a prior drought-year, not Exodus’s ten. No firstborn. No darkness as a named item. No Passover.
7:136–137 drowned; the weakened inherit

Vengeance: drowned in the yamm because they denied the signs and were heedless of them. The weakened inherit east and west of the land We blessed. The good word of your Lord fulfilled on Israel for their patience. What Pharaoh made and erected is destroyed. 2:50 already had the split-and-drowned-while-you-looked sentence. This panel adds inheritance of blessed land-parts and the ruin of Pharaoh’s works. Pharaoh’s last words in the water stay parked at 10:90–92.
7:138–141 a god like theirs

Across the sea they meet a people devoted to idols (yaʿkufūna ʿalā aṣnām). Make us a god as they have gods. Moses: you are ignorant; what they are in is ruined. Shall I seek a god other than God, who favored you over the worlds? He reminds them of the slaying of sons they have just left. The calf is not yet; this is a prior itch for a visible god.
4. Lemmas
sinīn. iṭṭayyarnā / ṭāʾir. ṭūfān. qummal. yamm. istaḍʿafū. mashāriq al-arḍ wa-maghāribahā. ʿakafa ʿalā aṣnām. balāʾ.
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Locus
Split among core five
Return to Arabic
7:133 al-tufan
SI: the flood. Haleem: the flood. Pickthall: the flood. Arberry: the flood. Yusuf Ali line: Wholesale death.
tufan is flood / inundation in the four. YA's 'wholesale death' is a minority gloss. Do not prefer it.
7:133 al-qummal
SI: lice. Haleem: lice. Pickthall: vermin. Arberry: lice.
qummal is small biting pests — lice / vermin / weevil in the lexica. Pickthall stays generic. Not Exodus's 'gnats' or 'flies' as a forced identity.
7:136 al-yamm
SI: the sea. Haleem: the sea. Pickthall: the sea. Arberry: the sea.
yamm = sea / great water. Same drowning already walked at 2:50 (bahr).
7:137 mashariq al-ardi wa-magharibaha allati barakna fiha
SI: eastern and western [parts] of the land which We blessed. Haleem: east and west of the land We had blessed. Pickthall / Arberry: close.
Not named Canaan in the verse. Blessed land-parts inherited by those who had been weakened.
6. Theological Findings

Son-killing is Pharaoh’s policy twice. Signs can be refused in advance. A five-sign list plus drought is this surah’s blow-file. Promise under wrath is not kept. Drowning is vengeance for denial and heedlessness. Inheritance follows patience. Crossing does not cure the wish for a visible god.
7. Internal cross-references
2:49–50 sons and drowning. 7:141 restates 2:49. 17:101 nine signs parked. 27:12 nine signs parked. 10:90–92 Pharaoh in the water parked. 7:148 calf next.
8. Biblical cross-references

Exod 1:16 / 1:22 son-killing. Exod 7–11 ten plagues (blood, frogs, gnats, flies, livestock, boils, hail, locusts, darkness, firstborn). Exod 14 sea. Exod 32 calf is later; this panel’s idol-request is a different scene (a people already devoted to idols). Josh / Num inheritance of the land.
9. Agreement / Difference
QB-0188 PARTIAL AGREEMENT: son-killing policy; flood/hail-cousin, locusts, pests, frogs, blood; drowning in the sea; a land inherited after.
QB-0189 CONTRAST of count and missing items. This list is five named plus drought-years. No firstborn, no darkness, no Passover, no boils/livestock as named items. Do not pad it to ten.
QB-0190 CONTRAST: after the crossing they ask for an idol like the people they meet — not the calf-scene, which is still ahead at 7:148.

Meccan Moses-cycle continued. QRQ-0004 rasūl vs king. QRQ-0001 no god but God after a visible rescue.

22. Next
7:142–156 — forty nights, the tablets, ‘let me see You,’ the calf begins.

packets.title: S007 Al-Araf CP07 vv142-156
paragraphs: S007 — AL-AʿRĀF — CP07
Unit: 7:142–156 (15 verses)
Translations: Arabic primary. Core five on split loci.
Date: 12 September 2026
1. Overview

We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was forty nights. Moses said to his brother Aaron: take my place among my people; put right; do not follow the way of the corrupters. When Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said: my Lord, show me; look at You. He said: you will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it stays in its place you will see Me. When his Lord disclosed Himself to the mountain He made it crumble and Moses fell down stunned. When he recovered he said: glory to You; I turn to You; I am the first of the believers. He said: O Moses, I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My speaking. So take what I have given you and be of the thankful. We wrote for him on the tablets of all things an admonition and a detailing of all things. Take them with strength and command your people to take the best of them. I will show you the home of the defiant. I will turn from My signs those who are proud in the earth without right. If they see every sign they will not believe in it. If they see the way of right-conduct they will not take it as a way. If they see the way of error they will take it as a way. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them. Those who deny Our signs and the meeting of the hereafter — their works have failed. Will they be repaid except what they used to do?

The people of Moses took after him, from their ornaments, a calf — a body that lowed. Did they not see that it did not speak to them and did not guide them a way? They took it and they were ẓālimīn. When they regretted and saw they had gone astray they said: if our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us we will be losers. When Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said: wretched is that by which you succeeded me after me. Did you hurry your Lord’s command? He threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head, pulling him to him. Aaron: son of my mother, the people deemed me weak and almost killed me; do not let the enemies gloat over me and do not place me with the unjust people. Moses: my Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy; You are the most merciful of the merciful. Those who took the calf will have wrath from their Lord and humiliation in this life. Thus We repay the inventors. Those who do evil deeds then repent after them and believe — your Lord after that is forgiving, merciful. When Moses’ anger calmed he took up the tablets. In their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord. Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time. When the earthquake took them he said: my Lord, had You willed You would have destroyed them before, and me. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did? It is only Your trial by which You send astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our walī. Forgive us and have mercy on us. You are the best of forgivers. Write for us in this world good and in the hereafter. We have turned to You. He said: I strike with My punishment whom I will, and My mercy encompasses all things. I will write it for those who fear and give the zakāt and who believe in Our signs.
2. Structural Analysis

142–145: forty nights; Aaron left in charge; speech; the seeing-request; mountain crumbled; tablets written. 146–147: proud turned from signs. 148–154: calf that lowed; regret; return; tablets thrown; Aaron seized; forgiveness asked; wrath on calf-takers; tablets taken up. 155–156: seventy chosen; earthquake; trial; mercy encompasses all things, written for the God-fearing.
3. Investigation
7:142–145 forty nights; you will not see Me; the tablets

Thirty plus ten = forty. Aaron is deputy: put right; do not follow corrupters. The Lord spoke to him (already 4:164). Moses asks to look. lan tarānī — you will not see Me. The mountain is the test: if it stays, you will see Me. Tajallā to the mountain; the mountain crumbles; Moses falls stunned; recovers; first of the believers. Chosen with messages and speech. Tablets: of all things, admonition and detailing of all things. Take with strength; the people take the best of them.
This is the walked seeing-refusal. Not ‘no one ever sees.’ The sentence is to Moses in this request. 6:103 ‘sights do not perceive Him’ already walked is the broader cousin.
7:148–154 the calf that lowed; Aaron; tablets thrown and taken up

After him, from ornaments, a calf — a body (jasad) that had a lowing (khawār). It does not speak or guide. They took it. They regret and ask mercy before Moses returns — that order is this telling’s. He returns angry, throws the tablets, seizes Aaron’s head. Aaron: son of my mother; the people overpowered me and almost killed me. Moses asks forgiveness for himself and his brother. Calf-takers: wrath and humiliation. Evil-doers who then repent and believe: Lord is forgiving. Anger calms; tablets taken up; in their inscription guidance and mercy.
Aaron is not said to have made the calf. Sāmirī is not named. Both sit in 20:83–98, parked. 2:54’s ‘kill yourselves’ is not restated here.
7:155–156 seventy, earthquake, mercy encompasses

Seventy chosen for the appointed time. Earthquake takes them. Moses: will You destroy us for what the foolish did? You send astray and guide. Mercy encompasses all things (wasiʿat kulla shayʾ). I will write it for those who fear, give zakāt, and believe in the signs. The next verse will name those who follow the messenger, the ummī prophet — leave 7:157 for the next packet.
4. Lemmas
arbaʿīna layla. khalaftanī. arinī anẓur ilayk. lan tarānī. tajallā. alwāḥ. jasad / khawār. alqā l-alwāḥ. ibn umma. wasiʿat kulla shayʾ.
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Locus
Split among core five
Return to Arabic
7:143 lan tarani
SI: you will not see Me. Haleem: you will never see Me. Pickthall: Thou wilt not see Me. Arberry: thou shalt not see Me.
lan tarani. Haleem's 'never' is a strengthening. Level 1 is refusal of this request. Do not turn it into a finished beatific-vision treatise from one verse.
7:143 tajalla rabbuhu lil-jabal
SI: manifested Himself to the mountain. Haleem: revealed His glory. Pickthall: disclosed His glory. Arberry: disclosed Himself.
tajalla. Glory is Haleem/Pickthall's extra noun. The verb is disclosure / manifestation to the mountain.
7:148 jasadan lahu khuwar
SI: a calf — a [mere] body which lowed. Haleem: a calf that made a lowing sound. Pickthall: a calf after his image which gave a lowing. Arberry: a Calf, a mere body that lowed.
jasad + khuwar. A body that lows. Not said here to be alive. Samiri parked.
7:150 ibn umma
SI / Haleem / Pickthall / Arberry: son of my mother.
Shared. Softens the address while Moses holds his head.
Yusuf Ali 7:143 line only: 'By no means canst thou see Me (direct).' Adds 'direct' — tafsir.
6. Theological Findings

Speech is granted; sight of God is refused in this request; the mountain cannot bear the disclosure. Tablets hold a detailing of all things. The calf is mute and guides nowhere. Aaron claims coercion. Mercy is said to encompass all things, then specified as written for the God-fearing who give and believe.
7. Internal cross-references
2:51–54, 92–93 calf already walked. 4:153 they asked to see God; thunderbolt. 4:164 spoken-to. 6:103 sights do not perceive Him. 20:83–98 Samiri parked. 7:157 next.
8. Biblical cross-references

Exod 24:18 forty days. Exod 31:18 tablets written with the finger of God. Exod 32 calf, Aaron makes it, tablets smashed, Levites slay. Exod 33:18–23 show me Your glory; you cannot see My face; cleft of the rock. Exod 34 new tablets. Num 11:16–25 seventy elders.
9. Agreement / Difference
QB-0195 PARTIAL AGREEMENT: forty, speech on the mountain, tablets, a calf from ornaments in Moses’ absence, tablets thrown, Aaron implicated, a request to see, mercy after wrath.
QB-0196 CONTRAST of the seeing-scene. Exodus 33: glory passes; face not seen; back seen. 7:143: lan tarānī; disclosure to the mountain, which crumbles; Moses stunned. No cleft, no back.

QB-0197 CONTRAST of the calf. Exodus: Aaron makes it and proclaims a feast. 7:148: the people took it; Aaron says they almost killed him. Sāmirī parked. No Levite slaughter in this panel (2:54 remains the other walked line).
10–12. Context, QRQ
Meccan. QRQ-0001 seeing God refused. QRQ-0003 tablets as written detailing.

QDISC-0342

QDISC-0343

QDISC-0344

QDISC-0345

Forty, tablets, calf, thrown tablets — PARTIAL AGREEMENT
Seeing-scene CONTRAST with Exod 33
Who made the calf; no Levite slaughter here
17–20. Dictionary, dossiers, provenance

Moses: seeing refused; tablets thrown and taken up; asks forgiveness for Aaron. Aaron: deputy; claims near-killing. God: speaks; discloses to a mountain; mercy encompasses; writes mercy for a defined set. Level 1: Samiri unnamed.
21. Summary
Speech without sight. A calf that lows and cannot guide. Tablets broken and lifted. Mercy named as encompassing, then assigned.
22. Next
7:157–171 — the ummī messenger; twelve tribes; Sabbath town.

packets.title: S007 Al-Araf CP08 vv157-171
paragraphs: S007 — AL-AʿRĀF — CP08
Unit: 7:157–171 (15 verses)
Translations: Arabic primary. Core five on split loci.
Date: 12 September 2026
1. Overview

Those who follow the messenger, the ummī prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel — he commands them to what is right and forbids them what is wrong, makes lawful the good things and forbids them the filthy, and removes from them their burden and the fetters that were on them. Those who believe in him, honor him, help him, and follow the light sent down with him: they are the successful. Say: O people, I am the messenger of God to you all, of Him whose is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but He. He gives life and causes death. So believe in God and His messenger, the ummī prophet, who believes in God and His words, and follow him that you may be guided.

Of Moses’ people is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice. We divided them into twelve tribes, nations. We revealed to Moses when his people asked him for water: strike the stone with your staff. Twelve springs burst; each people knew their drinking-place. We shaded them with cloud; We sent down manna and quails. Eat of the good things We provided you. They did not wrong Us; they wronged themselves. When it was said: dwell in this town, eat from it where you will, say ḥiṭṭa, enter the gate prostrate; We will forgive you your faults; We will increase the good-doers. Those of them who did wrong changed the word said to them for another. We sent on them wrath from heaven for their wrong.

Ask them about the town by the sea, when they transgressed the Sabbath: their fish came to them on their Sabbath day visibly, and the day they had no Sabbath they did not come. Thus We tried them for they were defiant. When a community among them said: why do you admonish a people God is destroying or punishing with a severe punishment? They said: as an excuse to your Lord, and that they may fear. When they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil and took those who did wrong with a wretched punishment because they were defiant. When they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden, We said to them: be apes, despised. Then your Lord declared He would send against them, until the Day of Rising, those who would inflict on them evil punishment. Your Lord is swift in penalty; He is forgiving, merciful. We cut them up in the earth as nations. Some of them are righteous; some other than that. We tried them with good things and with evil that they might return. A generation succeeded after them who inherited the Book. They take the goods of this nearest life and say it will be forgiven us. If goods like it come they take them. Has not the covenant of the Book been taken from them that they not say about God except the truth, and they have studied what is in it? The home of the hereafter is better for those who fear. Will you not understand? Those who hold fast to the Book and establish the ṣalāh — We do not waste the wage of those who put right. When We shook the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was falling on them: take what We have given you with strength and remember what is in it; perhaps you will fear.
2. Structural Analysis

157–158: the ummī prophet written in Torah and Gospel; sent to all people. 159–162: a just remnant of Moses’ people; twelve tribes and springs; the town-word changed (already 2:58–59). 163–166: Sabbath-sea town; three parties; apes. 167–171: scattering; heirs of the Book who take goods and say it will be forgiven; hold fast; mountain shaken over them.
3. Investigation
7:157–158 the ummi prophet written with them

Followers of the messenger, the nabī ummī, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Injīl. His work: command right, forbid wrong, make good things lawful, forbid khabāʾith, lift burden and fetters. Believe, honor, help, follow the light: mufliḥūn. Then a direct address: O people, I am God’s messenger to you all. Kingdom His. No god but He. Life and death His. Believe in God and His messenger, the ummī prophet who believes in God and His words.
Ummī is a split locus (§5). The verse claims a finding in the two prior Books. It does not quote a verse. 3:81 / 61:6 still the other written-prediction files.
7:159–162 remnant; twelve springs; the changed word

A community of Moses’ people guide by the truth and do justice — QI-0004’s cousin: not all of Moses’ people are the same. Twelve asbāṭ. Staff-strike; twelve springs; each knew their place. Cloud, manna, quails — restates 2:57, 60. Town: say ḥiṭṭa, enter prostrate; the wrongdoers changed the word. Wrath from heaven. Already walked in 2:58–59.
7:163–166 Sabbath fish; three parties; apes

A town by the sea. Fish come visibly on the Sabbath and stay away on other days. Trial because they were defiant. Three groups: those who transgress, those who admonish, those who ask why admonish a people God will destroy. When they forgot, He saved those who forbade evil and took the wrongdoers. When they persisted: be apes, despised. 2:65 already walked the ape-sentence without the fish-story. This panel supplies the trial-plot.
No biblical town-by-the-sea with Sabbath-fish is a match. Sabbath law is biblical; this narrative is not.
7:167–171 scattering; heirs of the Book; mountain canopy

A declaration: until the Rising, some will inflict evil punishment. Cut up as nations; some righteous, some not. Tried with good and evil. A later generation inherited the Book, takes nearest-life goods, says it will be forgiven, then takes again. Covenant of the Book: say about God only the truth; they studied what is in it. Hereafter better for those who fear. Those who hold fast to the Book and establish ṣalāh: wage not wasted. Mountain shaken above them as a canopy; they thought it falling: take what We gave with strength.
The raised mount was walked at 2:63, 4:154. This is the canopy-image of the same file.
4. Lemmas
nabī ummī. isr / aghlāl. asbāṭ. ḥiṭṭa. sabt. ḥītān. qirada khāsiʾīn. ẓallalnā ʿalayhimu l-ṭūr.
5. Translation Analysis (core five)
Locus
Split among core five
Return to Arabic
7:157 al-nabiyya l-ummiyya
SI: the unlettered prophet. Haleem: the unlettered prophet. Pickthall: the Prophet who can neither read nor write. Arberry: the Prophet of the common folk.
ummi. Range: unlettered / gentile / of the umm. Pickthall unpacks as illiterate. Arberry hears umma. Do not collapse the word to one English before the dictionary file is thicker.
7:157 maktuban 'indahum fi l-Tawrati wa-l-Injil
SI / Haleem / Pickthall / Arberry: written / described with them in the Torah and the Gospel.
maktuban = written. The finding is claimed. No verse is quoted.
7:166 kunu qiradatan khasi'in
SI: be apes, despised. Haleem: apes! Be despised! Pickthall: apes, despised. Arberry: Be you apes, miserably slinking!
Same sentence as 2:65. Literal apes is the wording. Allegory is tafsir.
7:171 nataqna l-jabala fawqahum ka-annahu zulla
SI: raised the mount above them as if it were a canopy. Haleem: made the mountain tower above them. Pickthall: shook the Mount above them. Arberry: shook the mountain above them.
nataqna = pulled / shook. zulla = canopy / shade-cover.
Yusuf Ali 7:157 line only: 'the unlettered Prophet, whom they find mentioned in their own (Scriptures).' Same claim, no quoted verse.
6. Theological Findings

A messenger to all people, found written in the two prior Books, who lifts fetters. Moses’ people are not one bloc. Sabbath can be a trial-device. A later generation can inherit a Book and still sell the next load of goods. The mountain-canopy returns as the demand to take what was given with strength.
7. Internal cross-references
2:58–59, 63, 65; 4:154; 3:81; 61:6 parked. 5:15–16 light and Book already walked.
8. Biblical cross-references

Deut 18:15–19 a prophet like Moses — the usual biblical hook claimed for 7:157; the verse does not quote it. Isa / Gospel ‘written of him’ claims are extra to this wording. Exod 17 / Num 20 rock-water. Num 11 manna/quail. Exod 16 Sabbath manna-rule is the nearest Sabbath-food law; it is not a fish-town. Deut 4:10–13 / Exod 19 mountain. No ape-metamorphosis in the Torah.
9. Agreement / Difference
QB-0198 POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of 7:157 with Deut 18’s prophet-like-Moses. The Quran says they find him written; it does not cite Deuteronomy.
QB-0199 PARTIAL AGREEMENT: twelve groups, rock-water, manna, quail, a mountain hanging over a covenant. CONTRAST: Sabbath-fish town and ape-sentence have no Torah narrative twin.
QB-0200 CONTRAST of Sabbath function. Torah: a creation-and-covenant day. 7:163: a trial in which fish arrive only on the forbidden day.
10–12. Context, QRQ
Meccan close of the Israel-cycle in this surah. QRQ-0003 confirmation of prior Books. QRQ-0004 messenger to all people.
